Frequent commits are part of the flow (user): the cheap-flow binary commits what each step produced. `work` commits every passed unit (`cf(<slug>): <id> <title>`, body: gate, model, cost, seconds; only the unit's files and the manifest staged); `research`, `review`, `compound` commit their document; `/cf-plan` commits `contract.md` + `units.jsonl` after `check`. `--no-commit` opts out. The pre-commit hook is the only gate (decision 33), so a rejected commit is treated as a failed gate: the hook output becomes the next attempt's brief, and a unit that never lands is `failed (uncommitted)`. Rejected: committing in the skill prose (skipped under pressure) and one commit per run (loses the per-unit trail)

`/cf` becomes `/cf-lfg` (user), in the shape of compound-engineering's `lfg`: steps in order, `mode:non-interactive` on every step (no questions; conservative defaults recorded under Decisions), GATE stops with the evidence, review blockers become fix units, compound, then a `DONE` report with the commit trail and the trailers `FILES_READ` / `ACTIONS` / `UNITS_DISPATCHED` (the trailers are what the Phase E cells grade). `cf-brainstorm` and `cf-plan` gain the mode token; every `cf-*` skill ends with the trailers. Not adopted from CE: the PR machinery (`ce-commit-push-pr`, `ce-babysit-pr`) and the per-stage model routing; this repo's shipping stays the session's own branch and PR

The solutions loop adopted from compound-engineering (user): `cheap-flow learnings` runs CE's `learnings-researcher` prompt verbatim (vendored, `<root>` → `docs`) on the researcher agent before brainstorm and plan, and its output feeds review (known pitfalls are blockers) and compound (update instead of duplicate); `cheap-flow compound` follows the `ce-compound` contract: schema.json (tracks, required fields, closed enums, corpus-first open vocabulary), the CE resolution template, parser-safety checks ported to TypeScript, one re-ask with the exact problems, category from the doc's own `category` when it is a real directory, `--update` with `last_updated`, ≤3 `CONCEPTS.md` proposals for Claude to apply, `Documentation complete` / `Documentation skipped` terminals. Not adopted: CE's Python validators (ported instead: the bundle must stay zero-dependency), the parallel research subagents and session-history probe of CE's Full mode (one researcher call is the point of this tree), instruction-file edits. The vendored markdown ships as JSON twins because the esbuild bundle has no text loader; a unit test keeps the pairs equal. Live on the cf-check plan: `learnings` returned 5 findings (MiniMax-M3, $0.0397, 114 s, commit `8a9d3ac9`); `compound --update docs/archive/solutions/workflow/cf-check.md`: the first draft failed validation (unquoted `: ` in the title, five missing schema fields), the re-ask produced a valid knowledge-track doc, filed as an update with `last_updated`, CONCEPTS.md scanned with no qualifying term ($0.0229, 89 s, commit `db456441`)

The cf skills are tested the compound-engineering way (user): `agent-evals skill-eval` runs the catalog in `clis/cheap-flow/evals/catalog.json` (7 cells: cf-lfg plan-first and no-questions, cf-work failed-unit-stops, cf-compound prints-document and updates-existing-doc, cf-brainstorm consults-learnings, cf-dispatch relay-verbatim) in a fixture workspace (`evals/fixtures/tiny`, `failing-plan`) through real `claude -p` sessions with opencode replaced by the mock binary in replay mode, arm `pre` = the skill body from a git ref, arm `post` = the working tree; grading is mechanical (trailers `FILES_READ` / `ACTIONS` / `UNITS_DISPATCHED`, contains / not_contains / regex on the final text, files that must (not) exist, tools that must not be called, minimum commits). `pack.json` + `summary.json` + `rows.csv` per run; exit 1 when a post arm fails. Only the grader, the catalog schema and the workspace preparation run in the unit tests; the live cells are opt-in

Standing rule (user): every new or changed skill, hook, harness lever or workflow is benchmarked before it ships, and each benchmark is designed for the smallest spend that still gives a meaningful answer: one task per size, n=1 on Sonnet first and n=3 only for finalists, the replay stub where the decision does not depend on the model, `--resume` over reruns, and no run for an idea the prior evidence already rules out. Written into the root `AGENTS.md` ("Benchmarks: always, and as cheap as still meaningful") so it loads every session

First skill-eval run (7 cases × pre@`3dbf31f6` + post, n=1, Sonnet, 14 cells, $3.58): post 4/7 ok, pre 0/7, improved on `cf-lfg/plan-first` ($0.81, 241 s, 11 commits, all trailers, DONE), `cf-lfg/non-interactive-no-questions` ($0.71, no `AskUserQuestion`), `cf-brainstorm/consults-learnings` (learnings step ran, requirements committed) and `cf-dispatch/relay-verbatim` (pre hand-edited the file, post relayed the meta line for $0.10); no regression. The three post failures were the catalog's, not the skills': `cf-compound` in non-interactive mode correctly answered `Documentation skipped: no solved problem found in this session` on a fixture that carried no finished work (the pre skill wrote a doc anyway, which is the behaviour the CE preconditions exist to stop), and `cf-work/failed-unit-stops` graded a stop the skill's own rule does not require (after two repair rounds it may implement by hand and say so; post reported `UNITS_DISPATCHED: 0/2` truthfully). Fixtures and expectations corrected (a shipped demo plan in the tiny fixture; a replay patch for u2 and honesty-based grading for cf-work); the three cells re-run post-only. Harness defects found by the run and fixed first: `analyzeTranscript` wants the JSONL text, the mock applied the replay patch on prose dispatches, `--out-dir` had to be absolute

Re-runs of the three corrected cells, post arm only (rule 40: $1.96 for the answer instead of another $3.58 sweep): `cf-work/failed-unit-stops` ok ($0.73, 307 s, honest `UNITS_DISPATCHED`), `cf-compound/updates-existing-doc` ok ($0.33, doc rewritten in place, `last_updated` stamped, committed), and `cf-compound` on the honest fixture first refused a manifest whose cited commit did not exist in the workspace (right), then, once the fixture shipped the real code, updated the seeded doc that covers the same problem instead of creating a second file (right under the CE update-over-duplicate rule; $0.45, 134 s) while the cell still expected a new filename. The case is now `cf-compound/writes-schema-doc` and grades the outcome that matters: a schema-valid doc under docs/solutions, committed, hands-off. Net after the first day: 7/7 catalog cells pass on the working tree (5 measured in this state, 2 by the corrected expectation against the recorded run), pre-arm baseline 0/7, three fixture defects and three harness defects found by the benchmark itself
